subject: Follow-up: Observability & Inference — competitive comparison and next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Observability & Inference — competitive comparison and next tests

Tom — great to speak earlier. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Key pain: your infra teams need consistent observability across hosted endpoints and private deployments (VPC). The ask: parity in tracing, per-route token/latency breakdowns, and an easy way to correlate errors/quality regressions back to prompt sets.

Where Redwood helps (summary):
- Unified telemetry across Hosted, Dedicated and Private (same tracing/span format).
- Per-request token + cost breakdown and model-level dashboards so you can measure unit economics by route.
- Built-in eval hooks to tie prompt sets to quality regressions + alerts.

Competitive note: hyperscaler endpoints give basic metrics (latency, error rate) but lack integrated token/cost breakdowns, KV-cache insights, and first-class tools for rollback/canary on inference variants. I attached a quick matrix comparing Redwood vs hyperscalers and other APIs.

Proposed next tests (short list):
1) Latency p50/p95/p99 comparison (1000 requests, 1/2/8k contexts) — baseline on your dev env and Redwood Hosted.
2) KV cache hit-rate test with a prefix-heavy workload to observe latency/cost impact.
3) Tracing correlation: send a noisy traffic mix and verify span/trace continuity from request -> model -> fallback.
4) Cost-per-1000-tokens comparison including batching and caching enabled.

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscalers.pdf (matrix), acme_observability_matrix.xlsx (test plan). Also link to the demo recording below.

Next steps we agreed:
- You to confirm which test environments we can access (dev cluster + a staging dataset by EOD Thu).
- Redwood to schedule the test run w/ Logan (solutions engineer) next week and share a concrete runbook.

If that looks right I’ll schedule the runbook session for next Tuesday (Dec 8) at 10am PT.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_vs_hyperscalers.pdf] [Attachment: acme_observability_matrix.xlsx]

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmerobotics.com>

Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Observability & Inference — competitive comparison and next tests

Thanks Marissa — that recap is super helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can give you access to a staging cluster (k8s) and a sampled dataset. I’ll confirm creds with Priya.
- For the latency test, we care about tail latency at higher concurrencies (50–200 qps). Can Redwood simulate those concurrencies for Hosted vs Dedicated?
- We also want to validate trace/span consistency when we use our in-house APM (Dynatrace). Will your tracing integrate or export to a format we can ingest?

Regarding hyperscalers: our preliminary PoC with CloudCo showed decent p50 but p99 spikes and no visibility into token-level cost. That aligns with what you called out.

Open question: procurement needs an SLA and minimum commitments — any guidance from Rafael on how you handle short-term proofs without long-term reserved commitment?

I agree to the test plan. Priya and I will try to confirm staging access by Thu EOD.

- Tom

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Observability & Inference — competitive comparison and next tests

Tom — looping in some technical detail for the runbook so you can validate quickly. Short list of what we’ll measure and how: 

1) Latency tests: p50/p95/p99 across concurrencies 10/50/200. We'll use your request traces to preserve distribution. Will report mean, stddev, and 99th with sample sizes.
2) KV cache test: instrument cache hit-rate metric and measure delta in tokens-per-response and cost.
3) Batching impact: run with 0ms/10ms/50ms batching windows to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
4) Tracing: we'll emit OTEL spans with request IDs and show mapping to your Dynatrace via OTLP.

I’ll attach the runbook (in Drive) and propose Tue Dec 8 at 10am PT for the session. If that works Marissa, I’ll send the calendar invite.

Cheers,
Logan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
